jobs.title: Data Analyst 3 (Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research)
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**
---------------

  

The Data Analyst 3 is a health professional having advanced knowledge of the data management activities of the Stem Cell Transplant and Cellular Therapy Program. The Data Analyst 3 coordinates and follows through on the entirety of the activities that encompass the reporting of patient and program data to the Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR). This requires mostly independent work with general direction from leadership. The Data Analyst 3 also assists the Quality Nurse Manager and leadership with data collection and submissions as they apply to the National Marrow Donor Program (NMDP), the Foundation for the Accreditation of Cellular Therapy (FACT), and other regulatory and research agencies as needed. \#CA\-SB


**Apply By Date** **8/17/2026 by 11:59pm**


**Minimum Qualifications \- For full consideration, applicants are encouraged to upload license and/or certification if required of the position**


* Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience or training
* 1\-3 years of experience reporting data to the Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR).
* Ability to work with electronic medical records (ideally Epic), chart reviews, and data extraction.
* Knowledge of hematologic malignancies and non\-malignancies.
* Administrative skills and ability to exercise good judgment.
* Initiative and resourcefulness in making decisions.
* Analytical skills to evaluate information, practices and procedures, formulate logical and objective conclusions and make recommendations for effective solutions.
* Communication and interpersonal skills to effectively correspond with the co\-workers, physicians, patients, caregivers, clinic staff, and other healthcare professionals
* Organizational skills and attention to detail so that large volumes of records can be accurately maintained and workload priorities can be determined in an appropriate way to accomplish a task or goal.
* Writing skills including the ability to compose reports and correspondence while utilizing correct grammar, spelling and punctuation as well as clearly documenting research data onto forms.
* Ability to meet the scope of the program with general supervision and with frequent changes in priorities and deadlines.
* Organizational skills in setting priorities, following through on assigned tasks and adhering to deadlines in a timely manner.
* Ability to work cooperatively as a team member in a diverse workforce.
* Working knowledge of various software systems.

**Preferred Qualifications**


* 3\-5\+ years of experience reporting data to the Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR).

**Key Responsibilities**


* 60% \- Cell Therapy Data Management
* 20% \- Auditing
* 10% \- Cell Therapy Program Reports
* 5% \- Regulatory Affairs Management
* 5% \- Other

**Department Overview**


The UC Davis Stem Cell Transplant and Cellular Therapy program provides hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, cell, and gene therapies to adult and pediatric populations with both malignant and non\-malignant disorders.


**Department Specific Job Scope**


The Data Analyst 3 works within the Data Management and Quality Team to lead the collection and reporting of information regarding cell therapies that is both legally mandated as well as volunteered via research.

HealthRIGHT 360 gives hope, builds health, and changes lives for people in need by providing comprehensive, integrated, compassionate care that includes primary medical care, mental health services, and substance use disorder treatment.
  
  

**Benefits and perks:**  

* HR360 offers a robust benefits package, including PTO, 15 paid holidays, commuter benefits, retirement plans, and more!
* Employees qualify for public loan forgiveness programs
* Training and professional development opportunities
* Work with mission driven, compassionate colleagues and make a difference every day in the work that you do.The required work schedule for this position is:


JOB SUMMARY
  
  

HealthRIGHT 360, a nonprofit organization and a family of programs, is committed to providing accessible and comprehensive healthcare services to vulnerable populations. Our mission is to tackle systemic barriers to healthcare and promote health equity for all. We offer a wide range of services, including mental health care, residential and outpatient substance use treatment, and primary health services. Additionally, we provide transitional support for individuals re\-entering the community after involvement in the criminal justice system. By integrating physical and behavioral health, we empower individuals to overcome challenges by addressing social determinants of health, fostering resilience, and facilitating recovery.
  
  

CalAIM is an initiative of the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) to improve the quality of life and health outcomes of Medi\-Cal recipients by implementing delivery system, program, and payment reforms across the Medi\-Cal program. A key feature of CalAIM is the statewide introduction of an Enhanced Care Management (ECM) benefit and a menu of Community Supports, which, at the option of a Managed Care Plan (MCP), publicly funded health insurance plans for low\-income citizens, can address the clinical and non\-clinical needs of Populations of Focus with the most complex medical and social needs.
  
  

The Lead Care Manager (LCM) at the ECM program will maintain a caseload of members served under the Managed Care Plan (MCP) providing care by linking the client with appropriate services to address specific needs such as: health benefits, mental health, substance use disorder, physical health, employment, family and children services, Justice\-Involved concerns, housing, community resources, outpatient substance use disorder services, and aftercare. This role will take part in Enhanced Case Management (ECM) in partnership with local Managed Care Plans, including San Francisco Health Plan, Anthem, Kaiser and the Integrated Care Clinic, as well as coordinate with providers to provide case management needs for the clinic’s patient population. The LCM is required to identify and engage with each member in the community, including the member’s home, service provider locations and other, various locations requiring outreach.
  
  

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  
  

**Client Care and Care Coordination Responsibilities:**  

* The Care Manager will be responsible for organizing patient care activities, sharing information with those involved as part of the multi\-disciplinary care team, and implementing activities identified in the Managed Care Plan.
* Identifying eligible people from within State Prisons, County Jails, hospitals, and other locations for enrollment into the MCP.
* Using multiple strategies for engagement, including direct communication with the member (and/or their advocates), such as in\-person meetings where the member lives, seeking care or is accessible; mail, email, texts, and telephone; community and street\-level outreach.
* Maintaining regular contact with all providers identified as part of the members’ care team, whose input is necessary for successful implementation of member goals and needs, including Justice Involved oversight.
* Ensuring care is continuous and integrated among all service providers and referring to and following up with primary care, physical and developmental health, mental health, SUD treatment, and necessary community\-based and social services, including housing, as needed.
* Providing support to engage the member in their treatment, including coordination for medication review and/or reconciliation, scheduling appointments, providing appointment reminders, coordinating transportation, accompaniment to critical appointments, and identifying and helping to address other barriers to member engagement in treatment.
* Responsible for engaging with a multi\- disciplinary care team to identify gaps in the member’s care and ensure appropriate input is obtained to effectively coordinate all primary, behavioral, developmental, oral health, Community Supports.
* Assist the client with intake by completing assessments as required by the MCP.
* Monitors client's progress toward achieving Care management treatment plan goals and provides treatment plan input.
* Assess the client’s Care Manager needs and completes all Releases of information.
* Connects the client to benefits, healthcare services, employment, housing, community resources, outpatient substance use services, and other benefits/resources available to the client.

jobs.description:
Description:
**JOB SUMMARY**

  

The On\-Call Inpatient Care Manager Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN) is a California\-licensed vocational nurse responsible for providing after\-hours medical management support under the direction of a Registered Nurse, Medical Director, or other authorized clinical leadership. The role supports utilization management (UM), care coordination, discharge processing, and urgent authorization facilitation when the Medical Management office is closed, ensuring continuity of care and compliance with applicable regulatory, accreditation, and health plan requirements.


Requirements:
**MINIMUM \& PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education/Training**


Minimum: High School diploma or equivalent required. Graduated from an accredited Licensed Vocational Nursing program.


Preferred: Additional training or coursework in utilization management, care coordination, or managed care operations.

**Experience**


Minimum: Six months to one year of clinical experience as an LVN.


Preferred: Experience in utilization management support, case management assistance, discharge planning, MSO, IPA, or health plan environments.


Any combination of educational and work experience that would be equivalent to the stated minimum requirements would qualify for consideration of this position.

**Certification(s)**


Current, active, unrestricted California LVN license.

**Skills, Knowledge \& Abilities**

* Understanding of utilization management processes and medical necessity documentation requirements appropriate to LVN scope of practice.
* Familiarity with medical terminology and basic ICD\-10, CPT, and HCPCS coding concepts.
* Ability to follow clinical protocols, guidelines, and escalation pathways.
* Strong organizational, time management, and documentation skills.
* Effective verbal and written communication skills.
* Ability to prioritize tasks and respond effectively during on\-call hours under supervision.
* Proficiency with electronic medical records, utilization management systems, and Microsoft Office applications.

**PHYSICAL, MENTAL \& ENVIRONMENTAL REQUIREMENTS**

  

The physical, mental, and environmental demands described below are representative of those required to perform the essential functions of this position, with or without reasonable accommodation. The role involves primarily sedentary work with extended periods of sitting, screen time, typing, and telephone use, along with occasional standing, walking, bending, and lifting of materials up to 20 pounds. The position requires sustained attention to accurately process clinical information and follow established protocols during on\-call hours, as well as the ability to work evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays in accordance with assigned on\-call schedules.

**PAY RANGE**


$34\.00 \- $37\.00 / hourly

jobs.title: Development Coordinator
jobs.description:
**POSITION SUMMARY:**

The Development Coordinator plays a vital role in advancing Haven Hills' fundraising and community engagement efforts by planning, implementing, and evaluating donor stewardship initiatives, database management, the Haven Hills Ambassador Program, special events, communications, grant support, and development operations within the Development Department. This position is responsible for creating an exceptional experience for donors, volunteers, ambassadors, sponsors, and community partners while strengthening the organization's philanthropic support, donor engagement, and community presence.

Working under the general direction of the Director of Development, the Development Coordinator exercises independent judgment and discretion in implementing fundraising strategies, developing donor stewardship initiatives, analyzing fundraising data and trends, managing the Haven Hills Ambassador Program, coordinating fundraising campaigns and events, and recommending improvements that enhance donor engagement, operational efficiency, and community partnerships. The position independently prioritizes projects, develops systems and processes that support fundraising operations, cultivates and manages an assigned portfolio of individual donors, and represents Haven Hills in building and strengthening relationships with donors, volunteers, ambassadors, sponsors, and community partners.

Within established organizational and departmental objectives, the Development Coordinator has the authority to prioritize assignments, develop and recommend fundraising and stewardship strategies, establish operational procedures, manage an assigned donor portfolio, and make day\-to\-day decisions necessary to achieve development goals while exercising sound judgment and discretion in carrying out the responsibilities of the position.

Through these efforts, the Development Coordinator plays an integral role in advancing Haven Hills' mission of empowering survivors of domestic violence and their children to build safe, independent, and violence\-free lives while contributing to the long\-term growth and sustainability of the organization's fundraising program.

**Essential Duties \& Responsibilities**

**Donor Relations \& Stewardship**

· Process and acknowledge all charitable gifts in a timely manner.

· Generate tax receipts and donor acknowledgment letters.

· Maintain accurate donor records in the donor database.

· Develop and implement donor stewardship strategies that strengthen donor engagement, retention, and long\-term philanthropic support.

· Track donor communications, meetings, and follow\-up tasks.

· Manage and cultivate an assigned portfolio of individual donors through personalized stewardship, relationship\-building, and ongoing engagement.

· Prepare donor profiles and briefing materials for meetings.

· Plan monthly donor stewardship campaigns.

· Develop and implement individualized cultivation plans for assigned donors and recommend strategies to increase donor retention and giving.

· Create and Support donor cultivation activities by coordinating meetings, preparing briefing materials, assisting with donor follow\-up, and helping identify opportunities to strengthen donor relationships.

· Identify opportunities to upgrade donor giving, re\-engage lapsed donors, and expand philanthropic support.

· Exercise independent judgment in prioritizing donor outreach and stewardship activities based on fundraising goals.

**Database \& Development Operations**

· Oversee the integrity and strategic use of the donor database (CRM) to support fundraising initiatives.

· Analyze donor giving trends, campaign performance, and fundraising metrics to identify opportunities for growth.

· Develop reports and dashboards that inform fundraising strategy and leadership decision\-making.

· Evaluate database processes and recommend operational improvements to increase efficiency and data quality.

· Conduct donor and prospect research to identify new funding opportunities.

· Ensure data accuracy and integrity.

· Track fundraising metrics and campaign performance.

· Assist with donor segmentation and prospect research.

· Support gift entry, pledge tracking, and reporting.

**Special Events \& Sponsorships**

· Assist in planning and executing fundraising and community events.

· Coordinate sponsorship fulfillment and recognition.

· Manage event registration and guest lists.

· Work with vendors, volunteers, and community partners.

· Assist with silent auction and raffle coordination.

· Develop event implementation plans that align with fundraising objectives.

· Manage sponsor relationships and ensure fulfillment of sponsorship benefits.

· Evaluate event outcomes and recommend improvements for future fundraising initiatives.

**Ambassador Program**

· Manage the Haven Hills Ambassador Program by recruiting, training, supporting, and engaging volunteer ambassadors who represent Haven Hills throughout the community and assist with fundraising, outreach, and special events.

· Develop and implement ambassador recruitment, onboarding, and orientation processes.

· Develop, manage, and evaluate the Haven Hills Ambassador Program to expand community engagement, increase public awareness, and support fundraising objectives.

· Coordinate ambassador participation in community presentations, speaking engagements, outreach events, volunteer opportunities, and fundraising initiatives.

· Maintain records of ambassador participation and evaluate program effectiveness.

· Foster positive relationships that encourage long\-term ambassador engagement and advocacy for Haven Hills.

· Recommend new community partnerships and outreach opportunities that support organizational fundraising goals.

· Evaluate program effectiveness and implement improvements that enhance ambassador engagement and community impact.

**Communications**

· Develop donor stewardship communications and recognition strategies

jobs.title: Contract/ Part-time Program Coordinator - Arts Instructor (Pacific View Arts Center)
jobs.description:
**The Position**
----------------

  

  

The City of Encinitas is seeking creative and dedicated Program Coordinator \- Arts Instructors to support engaging arts programming at the Pacific View Arts Center. Program Coordinator \- Arts Instructors develop and deliver lessons across diverse disciplines—such as visual, performing, and multimedia arts—to help participants learn subject matter and skills that will contribute to educational development, promote creative expression, and encourage social engagement. This role is ideal for experienced educators who excel at designing curriculum, leading dynamic classes, and creating welcoming spaces where participants of all ages can explore and grow. Program Coordinator \- Arts instructors report to the Assistant Center Manager.  

***Program Coordinator \- Arts Instructor is a part\-time, temporary position. Incumbents work less than 999 hours a year. Work schedules may vary and incumbents may be required to work weekends and evenings.***
**Examples of Important \& Essential Duties (included but not limited to)**
---------------------------------------------------------------------------


Examples of Important \& Essential Duties (included but not limited to):

* Develop class ideas, create lesson plans and establish goals for a variety of arts programs such as drawing, painting, mosaic, collage, fiber art, printmaking, photography, dance, music, graphic design, animation and commercial art etc.
* Instruct participants of all ages in group settings of up to 16\-32 participants at various ability levels in arts classes, workshops, and youth camps.
* Provide appropriate instruction and activities for participants to meet objectives and enjoy the creative process. Lead classes through engaging teaching techniques that demonstrate clarity and creativity with encouragement for participants to reach their personal goals.
* Coordinate with volunteers to assist with programs.
* Select and requisition instructional materials; maintain inventory records.
* Ensure that all spaces and classes are safe, welcoming, and inclusive to all participants.


Essential Job Functions

* Resolves unusual or difficult customer service requirements without the necessity of referral to program managers.
* Performs a full range of duties, which require the application of comprehensive and specialized knowledge regarding arts education and classroom management.
* Coordinates, plans, implements, and assists in the management of arts education programs in the absence of direct supervision.
* Instructs others from outside the department and program in the methods and requirements to accomplish Pacific View Arts Center arts education priorities.
* Operates with considerable independence in maintenance of assignments and special projects related to assigned area of responsibility and or arts discipline.

jobs.description:
Overview:
* **This position is open until filled with an initial application review to take place after August 21, 2026\.**
* **The salary for this position is $5,858\.67 \- $9,347\.58 depending upon qualifications and internal equities and is non\-negotiable.**
* **This position works an on\-site schedule.**
* **Please note that due to the potential for the contamination of study samples, the incumbent must be able to confirm that they are not exposed to active use or residue from tobacco, electronic cigarettes, oral nicotine, or cannabis.**

  

San Diego State University’s **Center for Tobacco and the Environment (CTE), co\-directed by Georg E. Matt, PhD, and Thomas Novotny, MD, MPH,** is an extramurally funded center established in 2022\. CTE’s mission is to prevent, reduce, and eliminate the toxic legacy of environmental pollution and harm to human health caused by decades of commercial tobacco sales and use. CTE is an open, community\-engaged, inter\- and transdisciplinary research center that serves the diverse communities affected by the environmental impacts of commercial tobacco. CTE provides an organizational platform for the next generation of research that seeks solutions to environmental contamination and human exposure resulting from decades of tobacco use, and contributes to California’s comprehensive policy initiatives to end commercial tobacco sales and use by 2035\.


CTE is home to a well\-established group of multi\-disciplinary scholars from different colleges at SDSU, including Sciences, Health and Human Services, Arts \& Letters, and Professional Studies \& Fine Arts, whose work focuses on the environmental impacts of commercial tobacco use. Researchers at CTE conduct multiple extramurally funded research projects focused on tobacco and the indoor and outdoor environment, including the *Thirdhand Smoke Resource Center* and the *Policy Research Center for Tobacco and the Environment*. Established in 2019, the mission of the *Thirdhand Smoke Resource Center* is to disseminate thirdhand smoke\-related information to the general public, stakeholders, and tobacco control advocates. The Resource Center’s interactive website is the primary dissemination channel, supported by a robust social media presence (i.e., Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram), webinars, and print material such as newsletter articles and press releases. The *Policy Research Center for Tobacco and the Environment*, established in 2023, has two main policy goals: (1\) reduce tobacco product waste to protect the environment from microplastics pollution and chemical leaching and (2\) protect indoor environments from thirdhand smoke residue. Both centers are funded by California’s Tobacco\-Related Disease Research Program.  

Under the general direction of CTE’s Director and Co\-Directors, the Program Coordinator II will provide **in\-person** day\-to\-day oversight of Center activities, including but not limited to operations, purchasing, and budgeting; planning, implementing, and disseminating research projects; supervision of staff and interns; community outreach and education; and preparing reports for policymakers and funders.  



Responsibilities: **Operations: 40%*** Oversee day\-to\-day operations of CTE, including Policy Research Center and the Thirdhand Smoke Resource Center.
* Participate/prepare reports for recurring administrative team meetings.
* Run regular staff meetings.
* Provide supervision of direct reports and interns.
* Oversee operations of (e.g., timelines, resources, deliverables) of Center projects including rapid response research projects and DIY thirdhand smoke testing services.
* Support administration of expenses, purchases, and other back\-office duties.
* Coordinate website, social media, and other communication operations.
* Support development and tracking of annual budgets.


**Planning: 30%*** Oversee planning for and execution of all rapid response research projects, pilot projects, educational programming, community events, dissemination, outreach, resources, and other activities, including DIY testing.
* Oversee community outreach and engagement, including dissemination of results to relevant policy\-makers and other stakeholders.
* Oversee tracking of grant milestones and goals.


**Program Administration: 20%*** Plan and coordinate recurring events such as the Community Advisory Board and Scientific Advisory Committee.
* Plan and coordinate community events such as educational webinars and town hall meetings with policymakers.
* Oversee other program planning necessary for the implementation of research projects, such as IRB applications and preparation of community meetings.

**Other Duties as Assigned:10%*** Other responsibilities as assigned by the Center Director.


Qualifications:
**Required Minimum Qualifications*** Bachelor's degree and/or equivalent training and administration work experience involving study, analysis, and/or evaluation leading to the development or improvement of administrative policies, procedures, practices, or programs.
* **Six years** of progressively responsible experience in office or administrative environment

**Preferred Qualifications*** Master’s, DPH, or PhD in relevant field (e.g., psychology, public or environmental health).
* Knowledge of environmental and health harms of commercial tobacco.
* Experience in tobacco prevention or advocacy.
* Experience running multiple research, evaluation, or service projects.

  

ADDITIONAL APPLICANT INFORMATION* Candidate must reside in California and live within a commutable distance from SDSU at time of hire.
* Job offer is contingent upon satisfactory clearance based on background check results (including a criminal record check).

**Job Announcement**


The Community Youth Center of San Francisco (CYC) provides education, leadership development, behavioral health, intervention, street outreach, and workforce development services to San Francisco youth and their families. CYC envisions empowering young people to reach their highest potential as individuals and to develop a positive self/cultural identity. Our mission is to empower and strengthen a diverse population of high\-need youth and their families by providing comprehensive youth development through education, employment training, advocacy, and other supportive services.

**Salary:****$30 \- $34 per hour**

**Reports to:****Program Manager**

**Status:****Full\-Time, Non\-Exempt (0\.50 FTE – JRELL; 0\.50 FTE \- TOPS)**  

  

**POSITION DESCRIPTION**  

  

Community Youth Center (CYC) is seeking a Program Coordinator to support the Job Readiness for English Language Learners (JRELL) and Transition Opportunities and Programs for Success (TOPS) programs. Under the supervision of the Program Manager, the Program Coordinator will provide workforce development, case management, college and career readiness, and youth development services to English Language Learners and transitional\-aged youth (ages 14–24\). The coordinator will help participants achieve their educational, employment, and personal goals through workshops, individualized support, employer engagement, and community partnerships.  

  

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Coordinate and implement JRELL and TOPS program activities in accordance with program goals and funder requirements.
* Recruit and enroll eligible youth and conduct participant assessments to develop individualized service plans.
* Provide case management, supportive services, referrals, and ongoing coaching.
* Develop and facilitate workshops on job readiness, career exploration, financial literacy, workplace skills, and college readiness.
* Provide college and corporate tours to expose high school and TAY youth to post\-secondary education and career pathways.
* Assist participants with internships, employment, job placement, college planning, and career pathway exploration.
* Build and maintain partnerships with employers, colleges, and community organizations to expand opportunities for youth.
* Maintain an up\-to\-date list of transferable college credits and employment opportunities aligned with participant goals.
* Recruit internship worksites and support employer and worksite partners.
* Coordinate career exploration activities, college visits, community service projects, and youth leadership opportunities.
* Maintain accurate participant records, data entry, documentation, and required reports.
* Monitor participant progress and program outcomes to ensure contract compliance.
* Participate in staff meetings, trainings, outreach events, and agency\-wide activities.
* Perform other duties as assigned by management.

  

**QUALIFICATIONS:*** Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university, or a minimum of two (2\) years of experience in workforce development, youth development, case management, or a related field.
* Bilingual in English and **Ca****ntonese and/or Mandarin**.
* Experience facilitating workshops and providing workforce, college, or career readiness services for high school and transitional\-aged youth (TAY).
* Experience providing case management, conducting participant assessments, and developing individualized service plans for youth and young adults.
* Ability to work effectively with ethnically diverse, low\-income youth and English Language Learners while supporting their academic, career, and social\-emotional development
* Experience working with San Francisco's diverse communities, community\-based organizations, educational institutions, employers, and private sector partners.
* Knowledge of job readiness, job search, job coaching, career exploration, and workforce development practices.
* Strong organizational, facilitation, interpersonal, and collaboration skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities independently and in a fast\-paced environment.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills and proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Zoom, and other technology platforms.
* Demonstrated professionalism, personal responsibility, positive character, and commitment to serving youth.
* Ability to lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and willingness to work occasional evenings, weekends, and outdoor events.
* Commitment to complying with agency health and safety policies and procedures.
